Definition: an Agagite or descendent (subject) of Agag
BiblicalUsage: Agagite means a descendant of Agag — and in Scripture it belongs to one man, Haman, the enemy of the Jews in Esther's day. Haman the Agagite plotted to destroy all the Jews, and Esther pleaded against the device he had devised; in the end he was hanged on the gallows he built for Mordecai.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the Agagite's story is the long shadow of Saul's disobedience. The king Saul spared left a line, and that line came back for the Jews in Persia — but God raised up Esther, and the gallows built for Mordecai held Haman instead.
